name: Utugwang-Irungene-Afrike
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Blench 2019 Atlas of Nigerian Languages (p.113, list entry) and Blench 2010 classification comment found; no grammar/phonology of Utugwang-Irungene-Afrike located

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, ed. IV. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 362 'Obe cluster' (pdf p. 107) and entry 'Afrike-Irungene cluster' (pdf p. 31).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: List entries only: Obe cluster (Obudu LGA, 16,341 in 1963; members Mgbenege, Utugwang/Otugwang, Okwọrọgung, Ukwortung) 'Refs. Otronyi et al 2009)'; Afrike-Irungene cluster (Ogoja LGA; Bantoid: Bendi) 'Refs. Survey: Otronyi et al. (2009)'. No wordlist, phonology or grammar reference for any member.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. n.d. 'Bendi materials' web page (rogerblench.info), Internet Archive copy 2015-04-20; plus the Internet Archive's index listing of the Bendi directory (2026-09-17).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists the only documents Blench holds for Bendi: Comparative Bendi (Blench), Obe cluster survey and Obe wordlists (Otronyi et al.), Bekwara grammar (Stanford), Bokyi wordlist (Jungraithmayr). Nothing descriptive for the Obe cluster beyond the two Otronyi items examined above.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2024. An overview of the Bantoid languages. Afrika und Übersee 97. doi:10.15460/auue.2024.97.1.288
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 4.2.6 Tones, Table 8: for Bendi only Bekwara 'H, M, L, four glide tones (Stanford 1967)'; no Obe-cluster data; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Change Request 2011-167 [afe], submitted 31 Aug 2011 by Zachariah Yoder, Linus Otronyi & Mike Rueck (Language Development Facilitators, Jos); rejected 2012-02-03. 6 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Naming request only (proposes Utugwang-Irungene-Afrike; dialects Utugwang, Okworogung, Mgbenege [m̀ŋgbénégè], Ukwortung [ùkwɔ́tɔ́ŋ], Irungene [iɾuŋɛnɛ:], Afrike); quotes Rev. Kierien Ayugha 2011; nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2010 [2001]. The Bendi languages: more lost Bantu languages? 32nd ACAL Benue-Congo workshop paper (Berkeley, 26-27 March 2001); draft dated Cambridge 22 Nov 2010, 26 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative wordlist/classification paper. Table 1-2 (p. 2): Utugwong 'includes Obe, Oboso, Okorogung, Okorotung', data from the handwritten 1960s 'Bendi mss.' (Bruns/Springer/Crabb) and a Williamson ms. for Afrike; p. 1 cites Chumbow 1986 on Ogberia (Obe dialect). Tone-marked datasheets only; the word 'tone' never occurs; nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Otronyi, L., J. Muniru, Z. Yoder, L. Hon et al. 2009. Obe cluster wordlists (NID2008-11 348-item list; Oboso, Ogberia, Eluka, Erimpang, Nkerira, Ukutia, Okpeche, Ochagbe, Ikpeng, Obadem, Eruche, Irayam, Itekpa/Bekwarra, Ekumtak/Mbe). Excel ms., last saved 16 Sep 2009; hosted on Blench's Bendi page.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Raw IPA wordlists with H/M/L tone diacritics (Utugwang 'tongue' ɑ̄bɔ̌ɾɔ̀, 'tooth' ìʃɑ́ŋ, 'hair' ìdʒì); no notes, no analysis, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Otronyi, Linus, Nengak Bako, Luther Hon, Carol Magnusson, John Muniru, Erika Peterman & Zachariah Yoder. 2009. A Sociolinguistic Summary of the Obe Cluster survey of Cross River State, Nigeria. Jos: Language Development Facilitators, June 2009. 18 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey (April 2009) of Afrike, Irungene (Mbube East/Mbe Afal/Obe), Utugwang, Okworogung, Mgbenege, Ukwortung. Sec. 1.3 (p. 8): 'Very little research has been conducted on the Obe cluster dialects and modern work that does exist remains unpublished or inaccessible.' No mention of tone, stress, accent or phonology anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent nil); bibliography (pp. 17-18) names no phonology of any cluster variety.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page putu1241 and reference pages 85153, 568513, 568597; Wikipedia 'Putukwam language' (raw wikitext); StressTyp2 dump (: 'afe' only in the ISO code table); archive.org full-text search for Utugwang/Utukwang/Putukwam/Okworogung (47/7/25/2 hits, all Ethnologue, thesaurus, atlas, index and mission-directory listings); Crossref and CORE queries for all variety names (nothing linguistic).
sources.note: Bibliographic and index listings only; no phonological description of any Obe-cluster variety is known to any of them.

sources.citation: Ayugha, Kierien Ekpang. 2009. Grammar write-up assignment --- Utugwang. Jos, Nigeria: Ms. 17 pp.

sources.note: The only descriptive item Glottolog lists for putu1241; a 17-page grammar write-up (probably a TCNN/NBTT course paper by the pastor who ran the Utugwang language project) is the one place a phonology/prosody remark could exist.

sources.citation: Yoder, Zachariah. 2014. The reliability of recorded text test scores: widespread inconsistent intelligibility testing in minority languages. MA thesis, Graduate Institute of Applied Linguistics (Dallas). xxviii+221 pp.

sources.note: Glottolog links it to the Obe cluster (dialectology); might reproduce survey wordlist data but is about RTT methodology, not phonology.

sources.citation: Otronyi, L. et al. 2009. Full (unabridged) report of the sociolinguistic survey of the Obe cluster of Cross River State, Nigeria. Jos: Language Development Facilitators.

sources.note: The 18-page summary abridges a full report that may contain the wordlist comparison and transcription notes; still sociolinguistic, unlikely to state stress.

sources.citation: Chumbow, Beban S. 1986. Nasality in Ogberia. Unpublished paper, West African Linguistic Society Conference, Ibadan.
